Invariant theory.fact: His proof used the Reynolds operator ρ from R to RG with the properties ρ(1) = 1 ρ(a + b) = ρ(a) + ρ(b) ρ(ab) = a ρ(b) whenever a is an invariant. Hilbert constructed the Reynolds operator explicitly using Cayley's omega process Ω, though now it is more common to construct ρ indirectly as follows: for compact groups G, the Reynolds operator is given by taking the average over G, and non-compact reductive groups can be reduced to the case of compact groups using Weyl's unitarian trick.
